newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey will soon tender for Iran gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Turkey will soon tender for Iran gas pipeline.

text.p: Turkey will soon open a tender to build a pipeline that will carry natural gas from Iran under a 23-year, $23-billion agreement with its gas-rich eastern neignbour, Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Monday.

"In the shortest possible time, the tender for the pipeline will be carried out," he told reporters after meeting Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, who came to Turkey on Monday for a three-day visit.
"Iranian minister came to finalise the details regarding the construction of the pipeline," he said.
Turkey and Iran signed an agreement in August under which Turkey will get an initial three billion cubic metres of gas from 1999 through a pipeline to be built from Tabriz to Ankara.
The amount will rise to 10 billion cubic metres from 2005.

"The world nations see the agreement as one of the most important and greatest agreements in this century," Aghazaden said after meeting Erbakan. "Our visit to Ankara aims to put the project into practice," he said.
The total length of the pipeline will be about 1,420 km (890 miles) long, of which 1,150 km (720 miles) will be in Turkey, according to preliminary studies.

The gas deal requires both countries to build the section of the pipeline through their territories in a move to avoid breaching a U.S. decision in August that non-U.S. investors putting at least $40 million in energy projects in Iran and Libya would be punished.
Officials have predicted the Turkish section of the pipeline would cost about $1 billion.
Under the gas deal Iran will have sold about 190 billion cubic metres to Turkey in the lifetime of the project.
Erbakan said gas purchases would boost Turkey's trade with Iran which he said would rise to $2 billion in two-way trade from the current level of about $950 million.
He said Turkey would build gas-fired power plants along the pipeline to feed industrial sites in the economically backward eastern provinces.
Turkey also began electricity imports from Iran in August, when Erbakan visited Tehran.
Its purchases, presently at 150 million kilowatt-hours (kWh) a year, will reach 500 million kWh next year.
